record.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt models for multimodal agents and local deployment
record.summary: NVIDIA announced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B open model for multimodal agent tasks, alongside Bolt 74B-A9B targeted at 24GB local deployment and Bolt E4B for 4GB devices. NVIDIA's Oct. 15 account said E4B was scheduled for Oct. 23.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NVIDIA announced release of Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, and two Bolt variants, with Bolt E4B stated as forthcoming on Oct. 23.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA describes Super VL as a 120B multimodal model, Bolt 74B-A9B as native 2-bit and designed for 24GB, and Bolt E4B for 4GB devices.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA reports up to 5x faster task completion/throughput versus models in its comparison class; the comparison is not independently assessed here.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent evaluations under matched quality, memory, throughput and task-completion conditions are absent from this bounded review.

brief.importance_rationale: If the stated capabilities and deployment tradeoffs hold, a 120B multimodal agent model plus variants targeting 24GB and 4GB devices could expand where open-weight agent systems can run and be adapted. This is consequential for inference access and evaluation, but announced performance and adoption remain vendor claims without independent measurement in this review.
limitations: Performance and speed statements are NVIDIA's own comparisons; comparison controls and independent reproduction were not verified here.
Partner customization and integration examples are reported by NVIDIA and do not establish adoption scale or outcomes.
Bolt E4B was described as forthcoming Oct. 23; availability was not asserted as of the Oct. 15 source.
brief.summary: NVIDIA announced Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B open model for multimodal agent tasks, alongside Bolt 74B-A9B targeted at 24GB local deployment and Bolt E4B for 4GB devices. NVIDIA's Oct. 15 account said E4B was scheduled for Oct. 23.

technical.claimed_result: NVIDIA claims high task accuracy and up to 5x faster throughput for Super VL; independent matched comparisons were not checked.
technical.compute_or_cost: No independently measured training or serving cost was verified in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: NVIDIA publicly announced Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B availability and stated a later Oct. 23 date for Bolt E4B.
technical.implementation_status: Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B announced available; Bolt E4B announced for Oct. 23, 2026.
technical.mechanism: A model family spans a 120B multimodal agent model and smaller memory-targeted Bolt variants; the vendor describes native 2-bit quantization for Bolt 74B-A9B.
technical.novelty: A single release announcement spans a large multimodal agent model and local variants designed around substantially smaller memory budgets.
technical.regime: Vendor-announced open model family targeting data-center, workstation and local/edge deployments; Super VL is 120B and Bolt variants target 24GB and 4GB footprints.
technical.reproducibility: NVIDIA links weights, datasets and recipes; their contents and independent reproduction were not assessed in this bounded review.
technical.strongest_baseline: NVIDIA's comparison class for open agentic models; precise matched systems and harnesses require inspection of the linked evaluation materials.

brief.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt models for multimodal agents and local deployment
brief.why_it_matters: The release pairs a large multimodal agent model with much smaller memory-targeted variants, giving researchers concrete open artifacts to examine across cloud, workstation and edge deployment regimes. The vendor's speed, accuracy and partner-adoption claims remain unverified.
